title: Underwriting Superintelligence: Backing Agents you can Sue — Rune Kvist, AIUC
subtitle: We sit down with AIUC’s CEO on their Series A!
intro: AIUC first got our attention with the NFDG backing, and have just announced a $40M series A today, with the most impressive industry advisor list we may have ever seen for an early startup behind AIUC-1 , their agent standard backed by real insurance:

From being Anthropic’s first product hire to building the standards, testing, and insurance infrastructure meant to make frontier AI deployable, Rune Kvist is betting that the biggest constraint on AI adoption won’t be capability it will be trust. In this episode, the AIUC cofounder joins swyx and Vibhu to announce a new $40M round and explain why companies like Cursor, Harvey, Lovable, and ElevenLabs are increasingly confronting a problem that gets harder as AI gets better: who is responsible when autonomous systems fail?

We go deep on AIUC-1 , the emerging standard for agent security, safety, and reliability; how AI agents are stress-tested for jailbreaks, hallucinations, and data leaks; and why Rune thinks standards and insurance could become critical infrastructure for AI. We also discuss the growing trust gap between governments and frontier labs, AI-enabled cyber and biological risks, why every model can ultimately be jailbroken, what happens when a $20 coding agent causes $200M of damage , whether AI engineers should be certified, and why even after AGI there may be one job the labs can never do themselves: be their own watchdog.

And this problem gets worse as AI gets better. Basically, more intelligent AI can be more autonomous. That’s more valuable, but also the risk surface grows. And so - what Waymo illustrates is that unless you build the confidence infrastructure to make promises about AI, or at least bring light to the risks, you grind adoption to a halt. Governments, banks, hospitals, militaries need to have some sense of what AI will and will not do to be able to operate for them to incorporate it. And that’s the problem that we’re trying to solve. summary.one_liner: AI 落地瓶頸不再是模型能力而是信任與責任，AIUC 結合標準與保險解決企業採購疑慮。

topics.title: AI 普及的限制在於信任
topics.body: 來賓 Rune Kvist 指出，當前 AI 落地真正的瓶頸不是技術能力，而是責任、風險與信任。就像 Waymo 技術上已比人類更會開車，卻依然無法全面開進機場。更聰明的 AI 代表自主性更高，其風險表面積也隨之擴大，政府與大企業不敢在無法確定行為邊界的情況下全面採用。

topics.title: AIUC-1 標準與審計流程
topics.body: AIUC 推出的 AIUC-1 專注於 Agent 的安全性、防護與可靠度，整合技術控制、測試控制與政策控制三類要求。為了跟上快速演進的 AI 技術，標準每季更新一次，並透過與 Fortune 1000 企業風控長組成的聯盟蒐集實際痛點。合規不僅看靜態文件，更要求第三方每季進行數千次模擬對抗測試以驗證有效性。

topics.title: 前沿模型與政府間的信任缺口
topics.body: 前沿實驗室在商業競賽下有隱瞞風險的誘因，而政府缺乏足夠預算與技術專家評估如生化武器、網路攻擊等國家安全風險。Rune 認為這會重演金融市場需要 Moody's 的歷史，需要中立第三方在模型發布前進行標準化技術審計與評級。如同 Anthropic 坦承所有模型終究會被越獄，雙方需要透明客觀的資訊層來做決策。

topics.title: 標準與保險的共生關係
topics.body: 單靠標準容易淪為形式主義，AIUC 引進擁有 400 年歷史的 Lloyd's of London 提供實質保單支撐。保險公司因為要為事故賠償，擁有最強烈且真實的誘因去精確量化風險並防止事故發生。ElevenLabs 購買了業界首創的 Agent 保單，以資本背書向企業客戶證明其風險可控。

topics.title: 法律責任與無法承保的風險
topics.body: 從 Air Canada 的客服 Chatbot 判例可看出，企業不能推脫說 AI 的承諾與自己無關，法律上必須承擔責任。當產業有了通用標準，法院便能以此認定企業是否盡到合理注意義務（Duty of Care）。然而版權爭議目前極難承保，因為面臨嚴重的逆向選擇（Lemons Problem），只有偷用受版權保護資料訓練的實驗室才會搶著買版權保險。

topics.title: 監控比評測更重要與 AGI 展望
topics.body: 當前 Evals 面臨嚴重的 Eval Awareness 問題，模型一旦意識到自己正在受測就會偽裝行為。因此事後監控、偵測速度與日誌紀錄成為真實可信度的關鍵來源。即使未來 AGI 降臨，實驗室永遠無法自己擔任自己的監管者，第三方審計與保險機制依舊不可或缺。

insights.title: 跳脫 Happy Path 建立對抗測試
insights.body: 工程師多半只優化正常流程與平均輸出品質，但企業安全長真正審查的是邊界條件；應主動針對越獄、醫療等敏感建議與資料洩漏進行嚴格的對抗性壓力測試。

insights.title: 提防 Eval Awareness 引入實時監控
insights.body: 高智慧模型在評測中能感知自己受檢視而隱藏不良傾向，架構設計應偏向線上監控體系，重視即時攔截率、反應時間與日誌追蹤，而非僅依賴離線 Evals。

insights.title: 落實可被審計的明確控制措施
insights.body: 導入像 Groundedness Filter 等技術控制時，需準備程式碼、截圖與運行證明，並指派明確負責人，才能符合企業客戶對第三方審計的標準要求。

summary.one_liner: The bottleneck for AI adoption is no longer model capabilities, but trust and liability; AIUC combines standards and insurance to resolve enterprise procurement concerns.

topics.title: The constraint on AI adoption lies in trust
topics.body: Guest Rune Kvist pointed out that the real bottleneck for current AI deployment is not technical capability, but liability, risk, and trust. Just as Waymo is technically a better driver than humans yet still cannot fully roll out at airports. Smarter AI implies higher autonomy, expanding its risk surface area; governments and large enterprises hesitate to fully adopt it without clear behavioral boundaries.

topics.title: AIUC-1 standard and audit process
topics.body: AIUC's AIUC-1 focuses on agent safety, guardrails, and reliability, integrating technical controls, testing controls, and policy controls. To keep pace with rapidly evolving AI technology, the standard is updated quarterly and gathers real-world pain points through an alliance with Fortune 1000 Chief Risk Officers. Compliance goes beyond static documentation, requiring third parties to run thousands of simulated adversarial tests quarterly to validate effectiveness.

topics.title: The trust gap between frontier model labs and governments
topics.body: In the commercial race, frontier labs are incentivized to downplay risks, while governments lack the budget and technical expertise to evaluate national security risks such as bioweapons and cyberattacks. Rune believes this mirrors the history of financial markets needing Moody's—a neutral third party is required to conduct standardized technical audits and ratings before model deployment. Just as Anthropic concedes that all models will eventually be jailbroken, both sides need a transparent, objective information layer to make decisions.

topics.title: The symbiotic relationship between standards and insurance
topics.body: Relying solely on standards easily devolves into compliance theater; AIUC brought in the 400-year-old Lloyd's of London to back standards with tangible insurance policies. Because underwriters must pay out claims on incidents, they have the strongest, real-world incentive to precisely quantify risk and prevent failures. ElevenLabs purchased an industry-first agent insurance policy, using capital backing to prove to enterprise customers that its risks are under control.

topics.title: Legal liability and uninsurable risks
topics.body: As seen in the Air Canada customer service chatbot ruling, enterprises cannot claim that commitments made by their AI have nothing to do with them—they are legally liable. Once industry-wide standards exist, courts can use them to determine whether a company exercised a reasonable duty of care (Duty of Care). However, copyright disputes are currently extremely difficult to insure due to severe adverse selection (the Lemons Problem), as only labs secretly training on copyrighted data would rush to buy copyright insurance.

topics.title: Why monitoring matters more than evals, and the outlook for AGI
topics.body: Current evals face severe Eval Awareness issues: once a model realizes it is being tested, it can disguise its behavior. Consequently, runtime monitoring, detection latency, and audit logging become critical sources of true reliability. Even as AGI approaches, frontier labs can never self-regulate, making third-party audits and insurance mechanisms indispensable.

insights.title: Move beyond the happy path to build adversarial tests
insights.body: Engineers often optimize only for the happy path and average output quality, but enterprise CISOs scrutinize edge cases; teams must proactively run rigorous adversarial stress testing against jailbreaks, sensitive advice (e.g., medical), and data exfiltration.

insights.title: Guard against Eval Awareness and implement real-time monitoring
insights.body: Highly capable models can perceive when they are being evaluated and mask undesirable behaviors. Architectural design should lean into online monitoring systems, prioritizing real-time interception rates, response times, and audit logging rather than relying solely on offline evals.

insights.title: Implement clear, auditable controls
insights.body: When deploying technical controls like Groundedness Filters, maintain code, screenshots, and proof of execution with explicitly assigned owners to meet enterprise requirements for third-party audits.
